note: Congenital contractures and arthrogryposis multiplex congenita (often involving distal joints like hands and feet) are consistently documented across reported cohorts with biallelic FILIP1 variants.

evidence.text: Five affected individuals from three independent families with homozygous truncating variants in FILIP1 presented with an overlapping phenotype including congenital contractures affecting shoulder, elbow, hand, hip, knee, and foot.

source.title: Homozygous loss-of-function variants in FILIP1 cause autosomal recessive arthrogryposis multiplex congenita with microcephaly
source.quote: Here, we report five affected individuals from three independent families sharing an overlapping phenotype with congenital contractures affecting shoulder, elbow, hand, hip, knee and foot as well as scoliosis, reduced palmar and plantar skin folds, microcephaly and facial dysmorphism.

evidence.text: Patients with biallelic FILIP1 variants presented with neurological defects, dysmorphic features, bilateral foot pronation, and flexion contractures of the fingers.

source.title: Bi-allelic variants of FILIP1 cause congenital myopathy, dysmorphism and neurological defects
source.quote: and bilateral foot pronation as well as flexion contractures of the fingers (i–iv).
